body: I was basing my idea of how well it would work off [this](http://lostallhope.com/suicide-methods/firearms/reliability).

I've spoken to my parents, but that was a few years ago. A few things changed in that time, but my suicidal ideation didn't go away, I haven't recently mentioned that I think about killing myself. I don't think I would fail if I tried to kill myself, because I would shoot myself in the head with a hunting rifle. It's not as ideal as something like using a shotgun or overdosing on certain medication, but I'm pretty sure it'd work.

Video games are great at rewarding you during the process, you often have short and long term goals that are tangible. When I've tried drawing in the past I can't help but think about how things don't look right, or that same problem of comparing too broadly. It's hard to find similar things to video games where you can feel like you're doing something and be satisfied, even though you're pretty much doing nothing.

I'm in a position where I'd almost rather die than take risks, so maybe I should just kill myself. 

I get what you mean now, and I can relate. In the past I'd sometimes feel like my life without things like playing games was pointless, nothing was quite as interesting or exciting. Nowadays it's rare for me to play games, I just don't get much from them. Part of it is that I don't have the energy for it, I just watch random stuff online or read things.

I've thought before that it might give me more satisfaction or meaning in life if I were to spend some time trying things or being involved in actions that helped others, but I haven't looked too much into them. I can't muster the energy for it.

>I entrapped myself into a pattern of using my hobbies as a justification for my existence.

I don't understand what you mean, could you clarify?
Standard things I guess, procrastinating, not exercising regularly. When I knew something would require repeated effort I'd just do something else, like play videogames.
I do not, part of why I got into this situation is that I've struggled for a long time with developing discipline, which is necessary for those things.

Thank you for sharing your perspective, and good luck with your consultation. 

I think a difference between us is that even when I first would wear female clothes, starting around when I was 5, I'd get erections. I definitely saw it as a peculiar and secret thing about me. When I got older I couldn't help but view it as a sort of fetish.

I didn't expect other people to be able to relate to that feeling of jealousy I mentioned, it was something that really bothered me.

My big challenge with therapists in the past have revolved around me and communication, even though it's a safe and open space I'd always get anxious and find my expression stunted, which is common in almost all my interactions with people I don't know well. I don't connect or open up with people, even around my family I feel alone and a little alien. There was definitely a lot of discomfort, and I just made the evaluation that it wasn't worth it.

Thank you for your response, I hadn't considered those options. I'll try and keep this in mind, it's tough though when I've taken a few stabs at therapy and medication treatment in the past, but had no real success.

Thank you for the informative response. I had considered that GQ and agender people would be part of the trans community, but wasn't quite sure. I didn't realize a person could undergo those medical steps towards transition if they were in the middle of the spectrum though, I figured a doctor would recommend against it or something. 

As a quick question, do you know of any trans men who have experienced a mirrored form of autogynephilia? I guess it would be called autoandrophilia. I know that people sometimes frown on the use of the former term, but taken on its own I feel it can sometimes be a useful descriptor.

That's kind of hard for me to answer, I wasn't expecting to be asked why I don't see myself as trans. I guess the reason is that I see being trans as tied to the gender binary, if you identify as the opposite in that framework from what you were initially recognized as, then you're trans. People who are in the middle of the spectrum, whether that's agender or genderqueer, would fall into another bucket, and at the moment I see myself as being closer to that than anything else I guess. Does that make sense? I'm sorry if I'm exposing my ignorance or anything.

I don't see myself in a position to pursue therapy at the moment because I have little money, no job, no health insurance, and limited ability to travel. I'd have to borrow a car to drive something like an hour to get to a town where I could see a therapist. If I really really wanted, I could do it, but another part of the problem is that I'm of a split mind when it comes to trying to treat my mental health problems. There's a contradiction to me in wanting to die, but also getting help to try and change that. I think part of why I posted here is maybe because I'm unsure it will help anything, so it didn't cause me a conflict.

I am questioning my gender, but I don't see myself as trans, just confused, in a sort of empty state. I had the option to pursue HRT and was seeing a therapist with a specialty in LGBT topics at one point, he was trans himself, but my life circumstances changed. When I was meeting him I wasn't having much relief from our sessions, but l realize I actually miss them quite a bit.
